title: Demo -- I build 121 in-game assets using Astra + reference-asset-compiler [RAC](MIT license) + Framewright (MIT license)
author: _raydeStar
selftext:
Hey all.  A few weeks ago I shared my reference-asset-compiler (RAC), a 3d pipeline for building assets on top of AI models to give the best fidelity outputs.  For this demo, I've created 121 assets in about 13-ish hours.  This includes getting all the assets created, textured, feedback given, re-rendering, etc.  Most objects in the demo were 1-shot, but a few had to be retextured, or some of the mesh got mangled.

I have continued that work forward, and wanted to share a progress report on everything.  Secondly, I developed a front-end UI that works along with RAC to view outputs, called Framewright.  

Here are the repos.  Both are open source:

RAC -- [https://github.com/raydeStar/reference-asset-compiler](https://github.com/raydeStar/reference-asset-compiler)

Framewright -- [https://github.com/raydeStar/framewright](https://github.com/raydeStar/framewright)

  
Really quick synopsis here, please ask questions if you've got 'em --

\-----------------------------

RAC

\------------------------------

Image-to-3d pipeline.  Supports 3d objects, texturing, rigging, animation, and tested specifically on the UE5 mannequin skeleton.  Work will probably have to be done to get it into Unity or Godot, but I tried to keep that minimal.

\-------------------------------

RAC Future Plans

\--------------------------------

Right now I am working on facial expressions and talking.  I am about 90% of the way there, I think, but there are still some issues I am working through.  

  
\--------------------------------

Framewright

\---------------------------------

I built this originally as a pipeline to create videos using Minimax H3.  I wanted to have a storyboard, a pipeline, and easily available hooks.  Afterwards I added the full setup for development -- 3d models, images, Audio (speaking), and music (YUE2 is plugged in right now) 

The idea behind this one, is to link mostly directly to ComfyUI and set up the workflows without you having to touch it.  When a new update comes across, when new workflows come, you can just ask Codex or Claude to pull it, set up the models, troubleshoot, optimize, etc.  Basically, it's a layer of abstraction above your existing framework, to get out work quickly.  Also, it supports linking in with Codex oauth, and you can have it create images for you. 

It also supports concept images and a wiki of characters you've made for consistency. This is all to say -- it's a planning board for video, image, 3d model, music, and voice production. 

\----------------------------------

Framewright Future Plans

\-----------------------------------

Someone online decompiled adobe projects and open-sourced them.  I am planning on onboarding a few pieces from there, so it can work in tandem with what already exists.  Mostly, I am interested in a more robust photoshop for images, giving our users more leverage over shaping a 3d scene, and overall borrow production-grade AAA concepts to make it feel like a good product.

\-----------------------------------

Workflow

\------------------------------------

Workflow for me was simple.  First, I asked Claude to build me a dungeon as a demo.  It took items that already existed, and placed them on the screen.  Then, I asked it to create a requisition request, and it did.  

I then passed it to Astra. Astra facilitated all the concept images, and models autonomously.  I was the approver.  90% of the models passed, but the more complex ones needed to be sent back.  Also, for things like the gems and metallic objects, I had it do a materials pass, to show the right reflectivity, opacity, etc.  

When everything was made, I sent it to UE5.  The video you see is after some spitballing back and forth with placement -- it was not a 1-shot process, but it was pretty close.  

\----------------------------------------

Thanks for your time guys!  I'd like to make this more useful for everybody -- very open to feedback!
